traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and technical requirements for story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are fully implemented and verified. The canonical rule name `traceability/prefer-supports-annotation` exists with `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` as a deprecated alias; the rule is disabled by default and can be configured with standard ESLint severities. It detects legacy `@story` + `@req` patterns, emits configurable recommendations, and provides a conservative auto-fix that rewrites single-story comments with one or more simple @req lines into a single @supports line while preserving JSDoc structure. Multi-story and mixed @story/@req/@supports blocks are detected and reported but not auto-fixed. Legacy @story/@req annotations remain valid when the rule is off, and even when enabled, many legacy forms are intentionally ignored, so both formats coexist safely. Documentation in docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md and user-docs/migration-guide.md provides migration guidance, examples, and configuration consistent with the story. Jest tests for this rule and related validation rules all pass, confirming behavior and output validity. Therefore the story is assessed as PASSED.
